From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

All — we’re ready to flip auto-rollback “on by default” for internal canary rollouts (not GA tenants). Before I schedule the enablement window, I need:

1) QA sign-off for the end-to-end path (synthetic breach -> evaluator verdict -> executor revert -> audit event -> console view).
2) SRE sign-off that paging/ticketing behavior is as expected for internal canaries.
3) Confirmation the feature flags + cohort targeting match the staged plan.

I attached the enablement checklist we’ve been tracking. Please reply in-thread with a “GO” or the specific blocker(s) so we can either proceed Thu or punt to next week.

Attachment: auto-rollback-internal-canary-enablement-checklist_v3.xlsx

Thanks,
Connor
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

---

From: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

QA status:

- Synthetic breach harness: PASS in staging (latency regression) and PASS (5xx spike). Verified traffic split reverts from 10% canary back to previous stable within ~2–3 minutes given current evaluation window settings.
- Console: verdict + rollback history panels show the rollback event and include the “reason” string.
- Audit: confirmed an audit entry exists, but I want a quick confirmation from Ethan’s side that the payload includes the policy id + rollout id consistently (we saw one run missing policy id in a retry path).

Remaining TODO before I can give a clean GO:
- Re-run once after merging the “unknown verdict / stale monitor” guardrail (I believe that’s PR-18546). We had a flaky scenario where the monitor endpoint returned empty, and I need to make sure we don’t rollback.

If PR-18546 lands today, I can re-run tomorrow morning and sign off by EOD.

Leila
QA Automation

Subject: Re: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

FYI PR-18546 is green in CI and should be mergeable. I’ll keep an eye on the integration test lane (the synthetic SLO breach job) since it’s been borderline on timing.

Also: the new job in PR-18529 currently runs on every commit to main after merge. That’s ok for now, but if we start seeing queueing, we may want to gate it to release branches.

-Sahana

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 2:04 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

On the audit payload:

- policy_id: should always be present for auto actions; we found one codepath in the executor where it was pulling from rollout ctx instead of policy ctx (only hit on retry). Fix is in PR-18488 already, and PR-18546 doesn’t touch it.
- rollout_id + target_version + previous_stable_version are present.

If you still see policy_id missing after re-run, ping me and we’ll grab logs from the decision trace.

Ethan
EM, Platform Control Plane

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

SRE/on-call perspective:

- For internal canaries, we’re OK with paging on auto-rollback *only* if the rollback repeats (flapping) or if rollback fails. The current alerting template looks aligned: auto-rollback event -> ticket; executor failure -> page.
- Please confirm the enablement defaults include:
  - min traffic guardrail enabled
  - warm-up window enabled (no rollback in first N minutes after rollout start)
  - cooldown enabled
  - “unknown verdict” does NOT trigger rollback

Assuming the above, SRE is a GO.

Rafael
SRE Manager

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

Connor — from Console/tooling side, I’m comfortable enabling by default for internal canaries once Leila signs off post-18546.

Answers to Rafael’s bullets (based on current config defaults in the checklist + what we reviewed in rollout plan):
- min traffic: enabled (internal canaries default threshold = 50 req / eval window)
- warm-up window: enabled (10 min)
- cooldown: enabled (30 min)
- unknown verdict: treated as “no action” (visible in console as Unknown)

One more thing: for the enablement comms, can we include the “where to look” links (console rollout page + runbook) in the change notice? The incident-bot formatting is good but folks will still ask.

Dylan
Console / Tooling

From: Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 4:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release readiness + QA sign-off — enable auto-rollback by default for internal canaries

Leila and I re-ran the “monitor outage / empty response” scenario after PR-18546 landed.

Results:
- Evaluator verdict went to UNKNOWN.
- No rollback action fired (as intended).
- Console showed “Unknown (monitor unavailable)” and the trace includes the monitor fetch error.

So reliability hardening looks good enough for internal canaries.

Connor: GO from me.

Miles
Staff SRE / Game Day Lead
